chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi, raising it from Hafs al-Awr, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'I take the rakwah (a type of vessel/pot). They say that if wine is placed in it, and the bukhtuj (fermented drink) is placed in it, it is better for it. So he takes the rakwah, places the wine in it, shakes it, then pours it out. Then he places the bukhtuj in it.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.الرَّكْوَة: A large vessel or pot, often used for storing liquids
key_terms.الْبُخْتُج: A type of fermented drink, distinct from wine
key_terms.الْخَمْر: Wine (or fermented grape juice), often considered impure in Shia fiqh
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use a wine vessel for other drinks after cleaning it by shaking and pouring?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on *khamr* (wine) as a liquid impurity (*najis al-ayn*) by permitting the reuse of a vessel after simply shaking and pouring out the wine, without requiring full washing. This indicates that for general consumption purposes, the physical removal of the wine is sufficient to render the vessel pure, reflecting the Shia view that wine's impurity is not permanent but requires only basic purification. The ruling underscores the practical ease of purification in daily life, distinguishing between the impurity of the liquid itself and the need for extensive cleaning rituals.
